## Problem and resulting behavior

Describe the concrete problem and final behavior. Link the issue or roadmap action. Fill this description before opening the PR, including a draft; update title/body when scope changes and remove prompts/inapplicable sections.

## Tracking and ownership

- Issue/action:
- Base/head:
- Existing GitHub labels matching scope:
- GitHub assignee: `@novakin` unless another responsible maintainer is named.

Set actual labels/assignee in GitHub; this template does not apply metadata automatically.

## Scope, privacy and compatibility

Identify affected collectors/runner/renderers, existing components reused, prerequisites, report fields/statuses and any compatibility decision. Explain evidence/privacy changes and operational effects. Do not attach host reports, scanner output or credentials.

## Verification

| Command/check | Revision/environment | Result, skips and limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| | | |

Record only checks actually run. Fixtures, native integrations, browser checks and live-host proof are different evidence. A passing suite with skips does not establish unperformed host behavior.

## Documentation and review

- [ ] Owning documentation matches the final source change.
- [ ] Relevant failure, cancellation, privacy and compatibility boundaries are checked or missing proof is disclosed.
- [ ] Affected HTML output was reviewed at relevant sizes/themes when applicable.
- [ ] Final diff is intentional and preserves unrelated work/evidence.
- [ ] Actual GitHub labels and assignee are set.
- [ ] Remaining risks and delivery state are stated below.

## Remaining limits and delivery state

State unresolved proof, risks and whether work is implemented, locally verified or deployed. A PR does not authorize merge/deployment. Keep the description free of connector/generated-by attribution.
